messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. They want:

1. In New York (NY), libraries with Reading Room and Fiction section.
2. In Los Angeles (LA), libraries with Wi-Fi and Children Section.
3. In Chicago (IL), libraries with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe". But the facilities argument seems to accept only one value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is union of those strings. That means we can only pass one facility at a time. But we need multiple. The function signature might not support multiple facilities. However, maybe we can pass an array? The description says "Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax." The type annotation shows facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. Wait, the last part "Cafe"[] indicates an array? Actually the type annotation shows "Cafe"[], meaning an array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Maybe it's a mistake. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby(_: { location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[] }) => any; So facilities can be either a single string or an array of strings? The union includes "Cafe"[] as a type. That suggests we can pass an array of "Cafe"? But that doesn't make sense. Possibly they intended facilities to be an array of strings from that set. But the type annotation is ambiguous. We can try passing an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc. Let's do that.

We'll call the function three times. We'll produce separate calls. We'll output the results.
